content:
Halloween season is officially here, which means that many are looking for a good scare for the spooky season. Visiting haunted buildings is one of the most popular ways to get the maximum amount of enjoyment out of Halloween.

This is a list of my 5 favorite paranormal buildings in Illinois:

Story continues below advertisement

  1. The Roff House/“The Watseka Wonder” 

The Roff House is located in Watseka, Illinois, and was built in 1868. The house is famous for being the location where America’s first case of spiritual possession was documented. 

In the year 1877, 13-year-old Lurancy Vennum endured trances and many psychological episodes. The girl claimed that she was possessed by the spirit of Mary Roff, the daughter of Asa and Dorothy Roff, who had unfortunately passed away. 

Nowadays, the home is restored, and you can book a stay through Airbnb. Visiting the property is like a time capsule since, with the restorations, it’s kept the same way as it was back in 1868. The home also offers Chef Valentino, who was professionally trained in Italy and makes gourmet dinners for guests. 

The home has such a rich and unique history that many guests have had the opportunity to experience it for themselves. 

  1. Old Joliet Prison 

The Old Joliet Prison is a famous haunted prison located in Joliet, Illinois, that operated from 1858-2002. 

The prison has appeared in different films, including The Blues Brothers and White Heat. 

During the Civil War, the prison was used to hold an array of criminals and POW’s. 

The prison’s conditions weren’t the greatest, as it was built to house 1,300 inmates, but despite this, the prison once held 2,000 inmates in 1878. This inevitably led to sickness and overcrowding in the prison and started popularizing the idea of the prison’s closure. 

This isn’t the prison’s only controversy, as there were also hepatitis experiments sponsored by the US Army occurring in the building during the 1960’s using draft-eligible inmates as test subjects. 

The prison housed many notable criminals, including the serial killer John Wayne Gacy. 

The prison eventually closed in 2002, but is now being preserved, offering many tours where you can explore the library, cafeteria, fire house, and cell houses. 

These tours are being offered throughout the month, including on Halloween. 

  1. Jane Addams Hull-House 

Jane Addams Hull-House is located in Chicago, Illinois, and opened in 1889, serving as a place to serve recent European immigrants, co-founded by Jane Addams alongside Ellen Gates Starr. 

One of the most famous legends of the property is the story of the “Lady in White”. The Lady in White is speculated to be the wife of Charles Hull (the original owner of the property), Millicent Hull. Reports claim an apparition of a woman in a white dress appears across staircases, gallery areas, and the Addams’ old bedroom. 

Another famous tale is the “Devil Baby Legend,” which started in 1913 after rumors spread of a baby being born and hidden within the house that had horns, hooves, and a tail. Thousands would crowd the building to catch a glimpse. Many believed this “Devil Baby” could speak fluently, cursing and mocking people. 

Jane Addams denied this, claiming the rumor spread out of a psychological outlet for immigrant women struggling with domestic abuse and raising children in severe conditions. 

You can currently visit the building now known as the Jane Addams Hull-House Museum, where you can attend tours and view the historic property. 

  1. McPike Mansion 

McPike Mansion is located in Alton, Illinois, which also happens to be deemed the most haunted small town in the country. One of the current owners of the mansion, Sharyn Luedke, was unaware the home was haunted when she first bought it back in 1994, but the woman claims she tripped on boards and bricks and also felt a tug on her jacket, which were supposedly the spirits keeping her from falling. She also claims that she could look up and see a mysterious man in her window. 

The mansion was built in the late 1860s, first occupied by Henry Guest McPike along with his family. McPike was a prominent figure in Alton, serving as a businessman and real estate developer. He even served as mayor from 1887-1891. 

The mansion houses many spirits, including Henry McPike himself and his first wife, Mary Amanda Burns. 

The current owners of the home, Sharyn and George Luedke, give tours of their haunted abode, with guests mainly seeking out the cellar, where many guests summon the spirits on the property. 

If you want to see the property along with the haunted cellar for yourself, there are still tours available every weekend in October.

  1. Ashmore Estates 

Coles County Poor Farm was built in 1916 as a place to house and assist the poor and mentally ill. After being sold in 1959, the building was converted into a psychiatric hospital, and the name of the building was changed to Ashmore Estates.

After struggling financially, the building officially closed in 1986. 

One of the most infamous tales surrounding Ashmore Estates is the story of Joe Bloxom. During the time the building was still a poor farm, Joe Bloxom was a resident of the building. One day, Joe was walking back to the property along some railroad tracks nearby before being hit by an oncoming train. Joe did not die here, however. Instead, he crawled or limped (depending on who you ask) all the way back to the doors of the building before tragically passing away. Other stories claim that his body was found and simply dumped onto the front doors of the property. 

It is said that his spirit, along with many other former residents and inmates, still resides on the property. 

In 2014, Ashmore Estates was sold to Robbin and Norma Terry, before being sold again in 2025 to Ashley Yvonne Burgoon. The property is still being taken care of today, offering tours and investigations during the day or, if you are more daring, at night. 

I myself visited Asmore Estates for a tour and can confirm there is a lot of history to the place. If there is one paranormal building to visit in Illinois, look no further than Ashmore Estates. 

Illinois has a lot of buildings with supposed paranormal activity, and the Halloween season is without a doubt the best time to visit these places, not just for a scare, but for a better understanding of the history that surrounds these places where many used to reside.
